tasks.short: Confer with staff on performance and company policies.

steps.what: Read the policy card before this housekeeping meeting.
inputs: the staff problem to be discussed
policy card when the office colleague has written one
outputs: the policy name and the one-line rule

steps.what: Confer with staff to resolve performance and personnel problems and discuss company policies.
inputs: the policy name and the one-line rule
the cleaner in the room
outputs: what the supervisor and the staff agreed

tasks.design: A paper policy card lists the policy name, the one-line rule, and who it applies to. The supervisor reads it, then still confers with the staff and still resolves the problem in the room. A missing row is the paper policy folder, read in the same lookup.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rule sat in a folder in the office, so the meeting started with a search.
tasks.enabler_now: Three fields on a handwritten card are enough. The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing the cleaner and resolving the performance or personnel problem stay a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the cleaner and deciding, in the room, how this problem is resolved.
tasks.altitude: Finding the policy is shorter when the card is current. The supervisor still confers and still discusses the policies with the staff.

reach.task: Keep the policy card the supervisor reads before the meeting
reach.learn: To write the policy name, the one-line rule, and who it applies to, and to drop a row that is no longer true

evidence.claim: Conferring with staff about a performance or personnel problem is a conversation. A card shortens finding the policy. It does not hear the cleaner or resolve the problem. Model knowledge.

A roster scheme, clock-in, and inspection results tied to named cleaners need works-council consent under the cited article, as does staff data. This meeting adds no roster scheme, no clock-in, and no inspection result. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited statute.

Recording sickness causes, and leaving absence records online without authentication, drew an authority fine in the cited case. This policy card has no sickness cause and is paper. Model knowledge of this design; the case is the cited report.

assumptions: The boundary is one meeting with housekeeping staff. Conferring and resolving the problem keep their full time.

Policy card fields are policy name, the one-line rule, and who it applies to. The producer is the office colleague, when a policy changes. If a row is missing or stale, the supervisor reads the paper policy folder inside the lookup.
The card does not name a cleaner's attendance or a mark. The agreement is made in the room. The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
Card upkeep is the office colleague's 1.0 hours per 100 supervisor hours on this task. The supervisor's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a small site has an office colleague who writes the card, or the supervisor copies the folder.
How often the policy the meeting needs has just changed.
research_questions: Of the staff meetings in a month, how many policies are current on the card, and how many problems are resolved only after the cleaner speaks?

incremental.description: The supervisor adds no recurring chore. Conferring and resolving the problem stay in the meeting above.
The office colleague writes the policy card by hand when a policy changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the policy card has no row, the supervisor reads the paper folder inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Conferring with staff never shrinks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate performance and recommend personnel actions.

steps.what: Read the floor note kept for this employee.
inputs: this employee
floor note when the lead cleaner has written one
outputs: the area, the date, and what was seen

steps.what: Evaluate this employee's performance and record what was seen on the floor.
inputs: the area, the date, and what was seen
the work the supervisor has watched
outputs: the performance judgement the supervisor recorded

steps.what: Recommend personnel actions such as promotions, transfers, and dismissals.
inputs: the performance judgement the supervisor recorded
the manager who hears personnel actions
outputs: the personnel action the supervisor recommended

tasks.design: A paper floor note lists the employee, the area, the date, and what the lead saw. The supervisor reads it, then still evaluates the performance and still recommends any promotion, transfer, or dismissal. A missing row is the supervisor's own walk of that area, done in the same lookup.
tasks.previous_blocker: What was seen on a shift sat in a pocket note, so the evaluation started with a search.
tasks.enabler_now: Four fields on a handwritten note are enough. The note is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
tasks.still_hard: Judging the performance, and recommending a promotion, transfer, or dismissal, stay with the supervisor.
tasks.human_edge: Judging this employee's performance from what was seen, and recommending the personnel action.
tasks.altitude: Finding the floor note is shorter when it is current. The supervisor still evaluates performance and still recommends the personnel action.

reach.task: Keep the floor note the supervisor reads before the evaluation
reach.learn: To write the employee, the area, the date, and what was seen, and not a mark, a rank, or a sickness cause

evidence.claim: Evaluating performance and recommending a promotion, transfer, or dismissal are the supervisor's judgement. A note shortens finding what was seen. It does not evaluate or recommend. Model knowledge.

A system that allocates shifts on behaviour or traits, or that scores workers, is high-risk under the cited annex. This task adds no scheduler and no score. The supervisor evaluates. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited annex.

A decision with significant effect may not be left solely to automation under the cited article. Promotions, transfers, and dismissals are recommended by the supervisor. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited article.

assumptions: The boundary is one employee evaluation. Evaluating performance and recommending the personnel action keep their full time.

Floor note fields are employee, area, date, and what was seen. The producer is the lead cleaner, after a shift on that area. The note has no mark and no sickness cause. If a row is missing or stale, the supervisor walks the area inside the lookup.
The recommendation in s3 is spoken by the supervisor to the manager. A change of what was seen voids any earlier reading of the note. The note is paper.

Works-council consultation is allowed in the consent range because the note names an employee. Card upkeep is the lead cleaner's 1.0 hours per 100 supervisor hours on this task. The supervisor's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether the lead cleaner will write what was seen, or only the supervisor walks the floor.
How often a recommendation is changed after the manager speaks.
research_questions: Of the evaluations in a month, how many employees have a current floor note, and how many recommendations change after the manager speaks?

incremental.description: The supervisor adds no recurring chore. Evaluating and recommending stay in the steps above.
The lead cleaner writes the floor note by hand after a shift, with no mark and no sickness cause.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the floor note has no row, the supervisor walks the area inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Evaluating performance and recommending personnel actions never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend changes that improve service and efficiency.

steps.what: Read the site note on how this building was cleaned.
inputs: this building
site note when the site lead has written one
outputs: the delay or the missed room, and the date

steps.what: Recommend changes that could improve service and increase operational efficiency.
inputs: the delay or the missed room, and the date
the manager or the client who hears the recommendation

tasks.design: A paper site note lists the building, the delay or the missed room, and the date. The supervisor reads it, then still recommends the change in person. A missing row is the client's written remark, read in the same lookup.
tasks.previous_blocker: What went wrong on a site sat in a remark the supervisor had to hunt before recommending a change.
tasks.enabler_now: Three fields on a handwritten note are enough. The note is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the change, and recommending it to the manager or the client, stay with the supervisor.
tasks.human_edge: Judging which change would improve the service on this building.
tasks.altitude: Finding the site note is shorter when it is current. The supervisor still recommends the change.

reach.task: Keep the site note the supervisor reads before a recommendation
reach.learn: To write the building, the delay or the missed room, and the date, and to drop a row once the problem is gone

evidence.claim: Recommending a change to service or to how the work runs is the supervisor's judgement. A note shortens finding what went wrong on the site. It does not choose or recommend the change. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one recommendation for one building. Recommending the change keeps its full time.

Site note fields are building, the delay or the missed room, and the date. The producer is the site lead, when a client remark arrives. The note does not name a cleaner. If a row is missing or stale, the supervisor reads the client's written remark inside the lookup.
The recommendation is spoken by the supervisor. The note is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
Note upkeep is the site lead's 1.0 hours per 100 supervisor hours on this task. The supervisor's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: How often the client's remark is already out of date when the supervisor reads it.
Whether the manager or the client is the person who hears the recommendation.
research_questions: Of the recommendations in a month, how many buildings have a current site note, and how many changes are dropped after the manager or the client speaks?

incremental.description: The supervisor adds no recurring chore. Recommending the change stays in the step above.
The site lead writes the site note by hand when a client remark arrives.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the site note has no row, the supervisor reads the client's written remark inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Recommending the change never shrinks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Screen job applicants and hire new employees.

steps.what: Read the application note before this screen.
inputs: this applicant
application note when the office colleague has written one
outputs: the name, the vacancy, and whether the person has cleaned a similar site

steps.what: Screen job applicants for the cleaning vacancy.
inputs: the name, the vacancy, and whether the person has cleaned a similar site
the applicant in the room
outputs: what the supervisor saw in the screen

steps.what: Hire the new employees chosen in that screen.
inputs: what the supervisor saw in the screen
the vacancy still open

tasks.design: A paper application note lists the name, the vacancy, and whether the person has cleaned a similar site. The supervisor reads it, then still screens the applicant and still hires. A missing row is the paper application, read in the same lookup.
tasks.previous_blocker: The application sat in a pile, so screening started with a search for the name and the vacancy.
tasks.enabler_now: Three fields on a handwritten note are enough. The note is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
tasks.still_hard: Screening the person in the room, and deciding to hire, stay with the supervisor.
tasks.human_edge: Judging the applicant in the room, and deciding whether to hire.
tasks.altitude: Finding the application is shorter when the note is current. The supervisor still screens applicants and still hires.

reach.task: Keep the application note the supervisor reads before the screen
reach.learn: To write the name, the vacancy, and whether the person has cleaned a similar site, and to drop a row when the vacancy closes

evidence.claim: Screening an applicant and hiring are the supervisor's judgement in the room. A note shortens finding the name and the vacancy. It does not screen or hire. Model knowledge.

A decision with significant effect may not be left solely to automation under the cited article. Hiring is decided by the supervisor after the screen. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited article.

assumptions: The boundary is one vacancy. Screening applicants and hiring keep their full time.

Application note fields are name, vacancy, and whether the person has cleaned a similar site. The producer is the office colleague, when an application arrives. If a row is missing or stale, the supervisor reads the paper application inside the lookup.
The hire is the supervisor's decision after the screen. The note is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
Note upkeep is the office colleague's 1.0 hours per 100 supervisor hours on this task. The supervisor's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: How many applicants arrive without a note the office has written.
Who else must agree before the supervisor's hire stands.
research_questions: Of the screens in a month, how many applicants are already on the note, and how many hires change after someone else speaks?

incremental.description: The supervisor adds no recurring chore. Screening and hiring stay in the steps above.
The office colleague writes the application note by hand when an application arrives.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the application note has no row, the supervisor reads the paper application inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Screening and hiring never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The supervisor still confers with staff, evaluates performance, recommends the personnel action, recommends the service change, screens applicants, and hires. A card only shortens finding the policy, the floor note, the site note, or the application.
reach: The office colleague writes the policy name, the one-line rule, and who it applies to before the staff meeting.
The lead cleaner writes the employee, the area, the date, and what was seen before the evaluation, with no mark and no sickness cause.
The site lead writes the building, the delay or the missed room, and the date before a service recommendation. The office colleague writes the name and the vacancy before the screen.
skills_to_grow: Open the paper policy folder, walk the area, read the client remark, or open the paper application when the card has no row.
Decide the personnel action and the hire from the person in front of you, not from the note alone.
role.ambitious_version: Cards do not confer, evaluate, recommend, screen, or hire. The supervisor still does.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Housekeeping and Janitorial Workers
